reader.requirement: The value an index-name holds must correspond to an occurrence number of an element of its table, the correspondence being the implementor's; the compiler must define one and apply it consistently wherever COBOL-85 lets an index be set, varied, compared, saved in an index data item or used as a subscript (direct and relative indexing), in one- and multi-dimensional and OCCURS DEPENDING ON tables.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry subscript-arithmetic-expression-2002: at 85 a non-integer data-name subscript is refused; not on the index-name value path
only the cited rule in COBOL1637 text (IndexNameRule Cite 1985/2023)

reader.edition-search: grep of SubscriptBinder.cs, PositionRenderer.cs, Model/Position.cs and Runtime/Values/CobolPosition.cs for Edition|CobolVersion|IsAtLeast|Dialect: the index cell (a long holding the 1-based occurrence number, initialized 1 in RecordStructEmitter) and its rendering as a position consult no edition; only the 1985 subscript-shape gate (VersionConformancePass / ConstructRegistry) and diagnostic citations do

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.4 GR2  (4.3.8.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2: This correspondence is defined by the implementor.

reader.notes: The implementor's correspondence is identity: an index-name is a C# long holding the 1-based occurrence number (docs/DESIGN.md and DATA_MODEL_DESIGN.md D3; docs/conformance/3/D-85-INDEX-IN-ANOTHER-DIMENSION.md states it for 85). ResolveSubscriptName returns the index cell (PositionIndexCell) and PositionRenderer emits the cell itself, so every use reads the same number; the removed OccScaled/RefModPosition members are now CobolPosition<TUse>.Read/Value plus CobolPosition.Digits, which carry numeric and non-numeric positions, not index cells. Every probe matched, and the 2023 run of the same program printed the same lines.

refuter.evidence: Probe probes-refute/src/r1ix.cob at --std 85 (runs/r1ix-001, EXIT 0) aimed at forms the reader did not try: SET UX TO IX across tables of different element size (C1 U4U4U4X), index-name of table A = index-name of table B (C2 EQ), USAGE INDEX item = index-name (C3 EQ), SEARCH U VARYING IX where IX indexes ANOTHER table (C4 DD U3U3U3X: IX advanced by the same occurrence count as UX), two USAGE INDEX items carried through a group MOVE and SET back (C5 DD U5U5U5X), a GLOBAL table's index set and read in a contained program (C8 AA, C6 EE after INNER sets 5), SET IX TO UX then UP BY 1 with relative - (C7 CC DD). Every value is the occurrence number, consistent at every use. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.4 GR2  (4.3.8.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2 ... This correspondence is defined by the implementor.' Members in code-location exist at 9bfe9e1c44 (grep). SubscriptBinder.cs edition consultations are the ConstructRegistry subscript-arithmetic-expression gate (line 144), the 2014 rightmost-ALL check (line 243) and diagnostic CiteRule text; none touches the index value.
